title: An integral number or a boolean header or query value is written as the one string that spells it.
why: behavioural spec 'request' (ADR 0019): a value that is not a string is written as the one string that spells it, but only where every language spells it the same way — an integral number becomes its shortest decimal form (no exponent, no trailing zeros, no leading '+'), and a boolean becomes 'true' or 'false'. A header or query value reaches the transport as a string and nothing else (shape spec §3.6), which is why the rule already writes a bare string as a one-element list.
note: This is what a test author means by `header("X-Count", 3)`: X-Count: 3 on the wire. The negative half of the rule — what is refused rather than spelled — is translation/unspellable-value.

interaction.description: counts and flags as header and query values
